title: Winter Tyres in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **There is no calendar date in the law.** § 2 Absatz 3a StVO requires winter tyres whenever there is black ice, packed snow, slush, ice or **Reifglätte**, frost slickness on the road. Von O bis O is a motoring club memory aid, not a rule.

**Berlin's road freezes about five weeks before the air.** Across the last thirty winters at Berlin-Tempelhof the median first ground frost is **30 September** and the median first air frost is **6 November**, a median gap of **35 days**. In 16 of those 30 winters the first ground frost fell in September.

**Since 1 October 2024 only the Alpine symbol counts.** The mountain-and-snowflake mark, 3PMSF. An M+S marking on its own is no longer enough. All-season tyres are fine if they carry the Alpine symbol.

**Tread: 1.6 mm is the law, 4 mm is the advice.** The ADAC recommends replacing winter tyres at 4 mm, and cold air costs you roughly **0.1 bar** of pressure per 10 °C, so check the pressure after the swap.

**The fine is the cheap part.** 60 euros and one point for driving on the wrong tyres in winter conditions, 80 with obstruction, 100 with endangerment. Your Haftpflicht can seek **up to 5,000 euros** in Regress, and Kasko can cut its payment for gross negligence.

**Side streets are gritted last.** The BSR clears city motorways, main roads, bus and tram routes and cycle lanes first. The pavement in front of your building is the owner's duty, often passed to tenants in the lease: **07:00 on weekdays, 09:00 on Sundays**, sand or grit only, never salt.
